question.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{′}+3y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $4$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+{{field-2}}\cdot sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$

current_example.problem:
Find the Fourier series of a particular solution of the differential equation

$$
y'-2y=f(x),
$$

where the Fourier series of the $6$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x) \sim 3 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{12}{n^2\pi}\cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{3}\right).
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
We assume that a particular solution has the following Fourier series:

$$
y_p \sim \dfrac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{3}\right) + b_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{3}\right).
$$

Now, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\  & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}))+{b}_{n}\cdot \frac{n\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for $y'_p$ and $y_p$ into the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\  & \,-2(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\  & \,\,=3+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{12}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -{a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{3}-2{a}_{n})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & \,\,+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{3}-2{b}_{n})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & \,\,\,\,=3+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{12}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, equating the free terms and the coefficients next to sines and cosines, we obtain the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{a}_{0}=3 \\ \frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{3}-2{a}_{n}=\frac{12}{{n}^{2}\pi } \\ -\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{3}-2{b}_{n}=0\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation,

$$
a_0=-3,
$$

which means the constant term is

$$
\dfrac{a_0}{2}=-\dfrac{3}{2}.
$$

Next, from the third equation,
$b_n=-\dfrac{a_n n\pi}{6}.$
Substituting this into the second equation gives

$$
\left(-\dfrac{a_n n\pi}{6}\right)\dfrac{n\pi}{3}-2a_n=\dfrac{12}{n^2\pi}
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
a_n=-\dfrac{216}{n^2\pi(n^2\pi^2+36)}.
$$

Therefore, for $b_n$ with $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{6} \\  & =-\frac{n\pi }{6}\cdot (-\frac{216}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36)}) \\  & =\frac{36}{n({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}∼-\frac{3}{2} & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,-\frac{216}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36)}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{36}{n({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36)}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$
